guides.title: Agentic Experience (AX) & Supervisory Governance
guides.description: Architectural discipline for supervisory human-AI control surfaces: four-tier autonomy ladders, Show-Your-Work derivation trees, 900s escrow gates, OBO privilege attenuation, and zero-displacement receipts.
triggers: designing AI agent approval or supervisory UI
replacing opaque AI chatbot automation with governed actions
adding undo, escrow, or delegation controls to AI workflows
auditing autonomous UI actions for human oversight
guides.overview: Agentic Experience (AX) treats AI systems as bounded operators under continuous human supervision rather than opaque conversational black boxes. Every agentic workflow pairs natural-language intent intake with deterministic execution previews, time-locked reversibility, attenuated credentials, and non-displacing status receipts.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Classify every AI action on the four-tier autonomy ladder

Never collapse passive suggestions, prefilled drafts, staged mutations, and policy-bounded loops into a single generic "AI Magic" button. Map each capability explicitly to `ADVISORY`, `SUGGESTIVE`, `SUPERVISED_AUTONOMY`, or `AUTONOMOUS_GOVERNANCE` and enforce matching confirmation friction.

### Rule 2: Separate conversational routing from deterministic execution

Use conversational UI only to gather ambiguous intent and clarify parameters. Once an operation targets live state, shed conversational persona into a deterministic "Show Your Work" payload displaying exact parameters, derivation lineage, and an explicit confirm or abort trigger.

### Rule 3: Enforce non-bypassable reversibility, delegation limits, and legal precedence

Stage mutating agent actions inside a 900-second time-locked escrow window with one-tap rollback and saga compensation, attenuate agent permissions via RFC 8693 On-Behalf-Of (`act` claim) scope ceilings, and fail closed with HTTP `409` whenever an active `LegalHold` protects the target record.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** assign every agent capability an explicit autonomy tier, reversibility duration (`>= 900s` for staged writes), and clear human escalation path.
- **DO** enforce `readOnlyHint: true` vs. mutating tool annotations on the server so read actions cannot silently write state.
- **DO** expose the model version, prompt invariant, policy bounds, and verification hash inside progressive `<details>` disclosures rather than burying them or dumping them inline.
- **DO** use `textContent` or DOM element constructors for all streamed or structured model output.
- **DON'T** let an AI agent confirm its own escrow proposal or escalate its own delegated OBO permissions.
- **DON'T** jump the viewport scroll position or inject normal-flow banners when an agent stages, mutates, or rolls back state.
- **DON'T** bypass `LegalHold` locks via agent confirmation, deletion, or purge buttons.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Verify mutating agent proposals enter a pending escrow state and expose a visible rollback trigger with `min-height >= 44px`.
  - Assert `Math.abs(scrollAfterAction - scrollBeforeAction) === 0` when staging or undoing an agent action.
  - Confirm `LegalHold`-protected records reject agent staging/mutation requests with HTTP `409` and display the statutory block reason in `#ax-receipt`.
  - Assert that `[data-tier]` never reports `AUTONOMOUS_UNRESTRICTED` when `act` (delegated OBO agent) claims are present.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Feature-detect `'popover' in HTMLElement.prototype` before calling `showPopover()` and toggle a `.\:popover-open` class with fixed bottom-end placement when native Popover is absent. Treat `<details name="ax-derivations">` as progressive enhancement; older browsers simply keep multiple panels independent without breaking disclosure access.

guides.title: Agentic On-Behalf-Of (OBO) Privilege Attenuation
guides.description: Display and enforce RFC 8693 On-Behalf-Of agent token scope ceilings so delegated AI copilots cannot escalate past human grants or bypass human escrow.
triggers: showing what permissions an AI agent holds on a user's behalf
preventing AI privilege escalation or chained agent delegation
designing OAuth token exchange consent or scope inspection UI
guides.overview: An AI copilot acting for a human user must never inherit unrestricted admin authority or mint broader credentials than its delegating principal. Under RFC 8693 On-Behalf-Of (OBO) token exchange, the agent's effective permissions are strictly the intersection of the human's grants, the server-enforced copilot ceiling, and requested verbs (`CRUDPA`), surfaced transparently in the UI.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Attenuate scope as the strict set intersection (`Human ∩ Copilot Ceiling ∩ Requested`)

Never grant an agent permissions the human lacks, and never allow a human admin's full privileges to pass through unattenuated if the copilot ceiling excludes destructive verbs. Compute attenuated grants server-side and ignore any client-supplied `AUTONOMOUS_UNRESTRICTED` override.

### Rule 2: Pin destructive verbs behind escrow and block chained agent escalation

Mark destructive operations (`D` delete, `P` purge) as `escrow_required_verbs` on the minted `act` claim so the agent can only stage proposals, never finalize them. Reject token-exchange requests where the incoming `subject_token` already contains an `act` claim (`403 RFC8693_CHAINED_AGENT_ESCALATION_FORBIDDEN`).

### Rule 3: Disclose exact delegated actor identity, TTL, and excluded rights in the UI

Before a user delegates a task, show a non-technical plain-English scope card alongside an inspectable breakdown: delegating human identity, `agent:*` actor ID, short token TTL (for example `180s`), permitted actions, and explicitly blocked actions.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** compute and display the intersection of human permissions and the copilot ceiling visibly before delegation starts.
- **DO** keep OBO access tokens short-lived (`<= 180s`–`300s`) and attach the `act` actor claim unambiguously.
- **DO** route any destructive verb (`D`, `P`) requested by an agent straight into a `PENDING_HUMAN_ESCROW` staging endpoint rather than direct execution.
- **DON'T** permit agent-to-agent token chaining (`subjectClaims.act` exchanging for another `act` token).
- **DON'T** trust client UI state or `autonomyPosture` flags in request bodies to widen agent capabilities on the server.
- **DON'T** expose raw JWT signatures or OAuth plumbing jargon (`RFC 8693`, `CRUDPA`, `AAL`) in consumer-facing Habitat A views; keep deep claim inspectors in technical audit panels or Habitat B.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Check all capability boxes including `D`, and verify `#obo-granted-verbs` never lists `D` or `P` while `#obo-denied-verbs` explicitly discloses human-escrow containment.
  - Backend integration check: submit a token with an existing `act` claim to the OBO exchange endpoint and assert HTTP `403` (`RFC8693_CHAINED_AGENT_ESCALATION_FORBIDDEN`).
  - Submit `autonomyPosture: "AUTONOMOUS_UNRESTRICTED"` in a delegation request and assert the server forces `HUMAN_IN_THE_LOOP_ESCROW`.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Built entirely on native `<fieldset>`, checkboxes, `<dl>`, and `aria-live="polite"`, requiring zero polyfills or external scripts.

guides.title: AX Exception Repair Tree & Blast-Radius Containment
guides.description: Visualize autonomous fault detection, failure classification, blast-radius containment scope, and dry-run saga recovery pathways using interactive accessible repair trees.
triggers: designing error recovery for failed AI workflows or tool calls
showing operators what failed and what stayed safely contained
adding dry-run fault simulation to an autonomous console
guides.overview: When an AI-orchestrated step fails mid-flight, generic "Something went wrong" banners hide both the blast radius and the automated recovery path. Render an interactive exception repair tree linking each failure condition to its exact containment boundary, zero-data-loss saga compensation step, and safe dry-run fault simulation buttons.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Map every failure branch to three concrete fields

Every exception branch must state: (1) trigger rule or threshold breached, (2) exact blast-radius containment scope (for example `Single Batch`, `Draft Only`, `Substation B`), and (3) deterministic saga recovery action guaranteeing zero data loss.

### Rule 2: Provide non-destructive dry-run simulation triggers

Include explicit fault-simulation buttons (`Simulate Latency Spike`, `Simulate Checksum Drift`) that highlight the matching tree branch, compute the dry-run compensation outcome, and update an accessible status summary without mutating production data.

### Rule 3: Pair visual tree graphics with semantic list or table fallbacks

Keep SVG repair diagrams clean and keyboard-accessible by syncing simulated selections to a semantic HTML status region and structured branch list so screen readers and narrow viewports read every path effortlessly.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** isolate dry-run simulations from live state so operators can rehearse failure recovery safely at any time.
- **DO** show both what stopped (blast radius) and what survived intact (`zero data loss`) on every fault branch.
- **DO** reflect active simulated branches via `aria-pressed="true"` on the simulation trigger and text updates in a live region (`role="status"`).
- **DON'T** expose raw stack traces, internal SQL exceptions, or database table names in frontstage recovery trees.
- **DON'T** rely on color alone (red vs. green boxes) to distinguish faulted vs. repaired branches; always include explicit status words and borders.
- **DON'T** trap users in a dead-end error modal with only "Dismiss"; always offer the next safe repair step (`Retry Safely`, `Switch Backup`, or `Revert Draft`).
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Click each `.btn-sim-fault` trigger and assert `aria-pressed="true"` shifts exclusively to the clicked button, the corresponding `[data-fault-branch]` sets `data-active="true"`, and `#repair-callout` announces the dry-run containment summary.
  - Assert zero network `POST`/`DELETE` mutations are dispatched when running dry-run simulations.
  - Verify all simulation buttons satisfy `min-block-size >= 44px` on `390px` mobile and `1440px` desktop viewports with `0px` horizontal overflow.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Semantic `<ol>` branch cards degrade cleanly at any viewport width without requiring complex SVG layout math; if you pair an SVG diagram above the list, mark decorative path edges `aria-hidden="true"` and mirror branch state into the semantic `<ol>`.

guides.title: Conversational-to-Deterministic Handoff
guides.description: Transition users from an empathetic Layer-1 conversational router into a persona-free Layer-2 deterministic Show-Your-Work payload and explicit confirmation gate.
triggers: turning a chat prompt into a live system change or booking
preventing LLM chatbot hallucinations during transactions
designing AI triage before form or API execution
guides.overview: Pure chat interfaces obscure exact parameters behind conversational prose, while bare multi-field forms intimidate users who still have ambiguous goals. Solve both by pairing a natural-language Layer-1 router that clarifies intent with a strict Layer-2 handoff that drops all chat persona and renders a deterministic payload, policy citation, and explicit confirm button.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Use Layer 1 strictly for intent disambiguation and parameter extraction

Keep conversational bubbles focused on clarifying constraints, missing fields, and operational boundaries. Never execute state mutations, payments, deletions, or external dispatches directly from a free-form chat reply.

### Rule 2: Shed persona completely at Layer 2 handoff

When intent resolves to an actionable command, transition into a utilitarian execution card or native `<dialog>`. Replace first-person AI phrasing ("I went ahead and scheduled...") with exact typed parameters, quantitative derivations, rule citations, and an explicit confirm or cancel trigger.

### Rule 3: Preserve two-way escapability across the handoff boundary

Allow operators to jump back from Layer 2 to Layer 1 to revise parameters without losing prior context, and never trap focus or scroll position during handoff transitions.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** validate parsed parameters against deterministic schema and domain bounds before rendering the Layer-2 card.
- **DO** expose the exact JSON payload or structured field table so operators verify what the backend will receive, not an AI paraphrase.
- **DO** put `autofocus` on the safe `Cancel` button inside the final `<dialog>` confirmation and reset `dialog.returnValue = ''` on `close`.
- **DO** return focus to `#intent-prompt` via `focus({ preventScroll: true })` when the user clicks `Revise Request`.
- **DON'T** keep conversational humor, emojis, or speculative filler inside Layer-2 execution cards.
- **DON'T** execute writes straight from an LLM text response without a deterministic review step.
- **DON'T** discard the user's Layer-1 prompt when stepping back from Layer 2 to edit an input.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Submit an out-of-bounds prompt (e.g., `1200 kW`) and assert `#l1-boundary-hint` explains the bound, `aria-invalid="true"` is set, and `#l2-execution-card` stays `hidden`.
  - Submit a valid prompt and assert `#l2-execution-card` becomes visible, `#l2-json-preview` renders valid JSON via `textContent`, and clicking `#l2-back-btn` restores focus to `#intent-prompt` with its text intact.
  - Open `#l2-confirm-dialog` and assert `Esc` dismissal sets `returnValue === ''` without executing commit logic.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Feature-detect `'commandForElement' in HTMLButtonElement.prototype` and attach a direct `showModal()` click handler when Invoker Commands are unavailable. If `closedby="any"` is unsupported, guard backdrop clicks with pointer coordinate bounds on `pointerdown`/`pointerup`.

guides.title: Four-Tier Autonomy Ladder
guides.description: Classify every AI feature into ADVISORY, SUGGESTIVE, SUPERVISED_AUTONOMY, or AUTONOMOUS_GOVERNANCE with matching UI confirmation gates, escrow timers, and stop handles.
triggers: deciding how much confirmation friction an AI action needs
labeling AI suggestions versus staged automated actions
designing multi-tier agent autonomy controls or mode switchers
guides.overview: Every AI-assisted workflow belongs to one of four discrete autonomy tiers: `ADVISORY`, `SUGGESTIVE`, `SUPERVISED_AUTONOMY`, or `AUTONOMOUS_GOVERNANCE`. Binding UI friction, reversibility windows, and server authorization checks directly to these four tiers prevents both silent destructive automation and unnecessary approval fatigue on read-only insights.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
Pick the tier that matches the blast radius and tool annotation (`readOnlyHint` vs. mutating/destructive).

### Rule 1: `ADVISORY` — Passive guidance with zero state mutation

Use when the model summarizes, classifies, or highlights risk without drafting or executing writes (`readOnlyHint: true`). Render inline recommendations with no mutation CTA and zero background side effects.

### Rule 2: `SUGGESTIVE` — Pre-configured payload awaiting explicit confirmation

Use when an agent prepares a concrete draft, diff, or form prefill with moderate impact. Require an explicit human click on an imperative commit button (`Apply Draft`, `Send Message`) before mutating persistent state.

### Rule 3: `SUPERVISED_AUTONOMY` — Staged execution inside a 900s holding escrow

Use for high-stakes batch updates, scheduling, or resource allocation where speed matters but human veto must remain open. Stage execution into a 900-second holding escrow with a live countdown, prominent `Pull Safety Switch (Undo)` handle, and server-side refusal if an AI principal attempts self-confirmation.

### Rule 4: `AUTONOMOUS_GOVERNANCE` — Closed-loop execution inside hard policy invariants

Use only for bounded closed-loop controls (such as rate throttling or thermal containment) governed by deterministic safety ceilings, multi-signatory pre-authorization, and an immediate `< 1s` kill-switch. Never grant unrestricted autonomy (`AUTONOMOUS_UNRESTRICTED`) to delegated agent tokens.

| Tier | Execution Authority | Reversibility Contract | Primary UI Control |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ADVISORY` | Read-only analysis | Not applicable (no write) | Inline insight + derivation disclosure |
| `SUGGESTIVE` | Human executes draft | Standard edit / cancel | Side-by-side diff + explicit Confirm button |
| `SUPERVISED_AUTONOMY` | Escrowed 900s timer | 1-tap instant rollback + saga compensation | Live countdown + Safety Switch + Bypass |
| `AUTONOMOUS_GOVERNANCE` | Policy-bounded loop | Immediate kill-switch (`503` circuit open) | Policy bounds badge + Emergency Halt |
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** expose all four tiers as visible radio options (`2–5` mutually exclusive choices) when operators configure workspace posture, rather than hiding posture behind opaque settings.
- **DO** bind UI tier contracts to server-enforced policy ceilings; the server must remain authoritative over what an agent token can commit.
- **DO** pair `SUPERVISED_AUTONOMY` and `AUTONOMOUS_GOVERNANCE` states with a continuously accessible abort or kill-switch control (`>= 44px` hitbox).
- **DON'T** execute `SUPERVISED_AUTONOMY` mutations directly without staging a reversible escrow window (`>= 900s`) unless an authenticated human principal explicitly confirms.
- **DON'T** accept client-supplied `autonomyPosture: "AUTONOMOUS_UNRESTRICTED"` overrides in API payloads or MCP calls.
- **DON'T** label `ADVISORY` read-only insights with mutation verbs like "Auto-Fixed" or "Applied".
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Verify switching between all four radio inputs updates `#tier-summary`, `#tier-primary-action`, and `#tier-halt-action` visibility synchronously with `0` console errors.
  - Assert that `ADVISORY` hides `#tier-halt-action` and never fires mutating `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` requests.
  - Assert that `SUPERVISED_AUTONOMY` and `AUTONOMOUS_GOVERNANCE` expose a visible `#tier-halt-action` button whose bounding box meets `width >= 44` and `height >= 44`.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Native `<fieldset>`, `<legend>`, `<input type="radio">`, and `[hidden]` work in all browsers without polyfills. Always use explicit `textContent` updates instead of HTML templates.

guides.title: Show-Your-Work Derivation Trees
guides.description: Expose AI reasoning lineage—prompt invariant, model family, policy constraints, intermediate hypotheses, and verification hash—inside native exclusive <details name=\"ax-derivations\"> accordions.
triggers: explaining how an AI calculated a number or recommendation
building an inspectable AI reasoning trace without clutter
auditing model parameters and policy bounds in the UI
guides.overview: Black-box AI scores and recommendations erode operator trust because users cannot verify inputs, constraints, or math. Surface the complete calculation lineage—prompt invariant, model metadata, policy bounds, intermediate steps, and verification digest—inside native `<details name="ax-derivations">` accordions that stay collapsed at rest and unfold cleanly on demand.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Surface all six lineage nodes inside the derivation disclosure

Every non-trivial AI calculation or policy decision must disclose: (1) prompt invariant or rule objective, (2) model family and deterministic parameters (such as temperature), (3) enforced policy constraints, (4) intermediate hypotheses or arithmetic steps, (5) rejected alternatives where relevant, and (6) the verification digest.

### Rule 2: Use native `<details name="ax-derivations">` for single-open step inspection

Group derivation panels with a shared `name="ax-derivations"` attribute so browsers enforce single-open exclusivity without custom JavaScript state machines. Never nest `<h2>`–`<h6>` elements inside `<summary>`, because screen readers expose `<summary>` with button semantics and strip child heading roles.

### Rule 3: Keep derivation prose scannable and DOM-safe

Render intermediate values with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` inside semantic `<dl>` or `<ol>` lists, and populate model-supplied steps strictly via `textContent`.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** include units, formulas, and numerical intermediate steps rather than vague confidence percentages alone.
- **DO** keep `<summary>` text plain (using `<span>` elements for title/status) and enforce `min-block-size: 44px` for comfortable touch and keyboard activation.
- **DO** use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on every numerical derivation row so digits align cleanly.
- **DON'T** place heading elements (`<h2>`, `<h3>`, etc.) inside `<summary>`; VoiceOver, JAWS, and TalkBack suppress child heading roles inside disclosure buttons.
- **DON'T** invent fake verification hashes or static confidence strings disconnected from actual computed values.
- **DON'T** auto-expand in-flow derivation `<details>` panels while a user is typing in a nearby search field (route live search matches to a top-layer anchored popover instead).
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Verify all `<details name="ax-derivations">` elements remain collapsed (`open === false`) on initial load, preserving compact resting height.
  - Click Step 1's `<summary>`, assert `step1.open === true`; click Step 2's `<summary>`, assert `step2.open === true` and `step1.open === false` in browsers supporting `[name]` exclusive `<details>`.
  - Assert zero `<h1>`–`<h6>` descendants exist inside any `<summary>` element.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Native `<details name="...">` exclusive accordions are Baseline Newly Available (2024). In older engines that ignore `name`, each `<details>` still opens and closes cleanly as an independent disclosure, or a 6-line `toggle` capture listener can close sibling `details[name="ax-derivations"]` items if strict single-open behavior is required.

guides.title: Time-Locked Autonomy Escrow Gate
guides.description: Gate mutating AI agent proposals in a 900-second holding escrow with live countdown, explicit human principal confirmation, HTTP 409 LegalHold dominance, and one-tap saga rollback.
triggers: building an approval countdown or undo safety window for AI actions
preventing an AI agent from confirming or deleting records under legal hold
implementing reversible escrow and compensating rollback for agent mutations
guides.overview: High-impact AI proposals must never mutate canonical records silently or permanently on first dispatch. Stage every mutating agent proposal inside a `900`-second (15-minute) holding escrow (`PENDING_HUMAN_ESCROW`) that refuses agent self-confirmation, yields strictly to active `LegalHold` locks with HTTP `409`, and preserves one-tap abort or post-execution saga compensation.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Hold pending mutations in a 900-second time-locked escrow window

When an agent proposes a `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, or `DELETE` operation, stage a pending escrow record with a `900s` expiry (`expiresAtUtc`) and surface a live `tabular-nums` countdown. If the window expires unconfirmed, transition cleanly to `EXPIRED_ABORTED` (`410 ESCROW_PROPOSAL_EXPIRED`) with zero state mutation.

### Rule 2: Enforce human principal confirmation and `LegalHold` HTTP `409` dominance

Reject confirmation calls from delegated agent tokens carrying an `act` claim (`403 AGENT_SELF_CONFIRM_ESCROW_FORBIDDEN`); only an authenticated human principal may confirm. Before staging, updating, or purging any record, check `LegalHold`: an active hold dominates all escrow staging, updates, and deletions, returning HTTP `409` (`K0_05_LEGAL_HOLD_ACTIVE_BLOCKS_ESCROW` / `_MUTATION` / `_PURGE`).

### Rule 3: Separate pre-commit abort from post-commit saga compensation

During `PENDING_HUMAN_ESCROW`, one-tap rollback marks the proposal `ROLLED_BACK_ABORTED` with zero side effects. Once `HUMAN_CONFIRMED_EXECUTED`, refuse fake no-op aborts (`409`) and trigger explicit saga reverse compensation from the captured `preMutationRecordSnapshot` (`ROLLED_BACK_COMPENSATED`), or block rollback honestly (`409 ESCROW_ALREADY_EXECUTED_IRREVERSIBLE`) if irreversible erasure already ran.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** display the remaining escrow duration using `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so countdown digits never jitter horizontally every second.
- **DO** enforce `LegalHold` checks before both escrow staging and final commit/purge, surfacing HTTP `409` status explanations immediately in an accessible live region.
- **DO** record a deep copy of `preMutationRecordSnapshot` on commit so post-confirmation rollback runs authentic compensating writes and emits a compensation event.
- **DO** separate the `Pull Safety Switch` abort button from `Confirm` with clear visual spacing (`>= 12px`) to prevent accidental slip clicks.
- **DON'T** auto-commit `DELETE` or `PURGE` actions when the 900s timer reaches `00:00`; expiration must fail safe to `EXPIRED_ABORTED`.
- **DON'T** allow an agent token (`claims.act`) to invoke the confirmation or post-commit compensation endpoint.
- **DON'T** report an already-executed mutation as "Aborted without side effects"; always distinguish `ROLLED_BACK_ABORTED` from `ROLLED_BACK_COMPENSATED`.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Verify initial countdown renders `15:00` (`900s`) in `#ax-escrow-countdown` and ticks downward while `PENDING_HUMAN_ESCROW`.
  - Toggle `#legal-hold-checkbox` ON, click `#btn-ax-execute-confirm`, and assert HTTP `409` / `LEGAL_HOLD_ACTIVE` message appears in `#escrow-status-line` while `state.liveRecord` remains untouched.
  - Toggle `#legal-hold-checkbox` OFF, confirm, then click `#btn-ax-abort-rollback` and assert `#escrow-status-line` confirms saga reverse compensation restored the pre-mutation snapshot.
- **Browser fallbacks:** `<output>`, `role="status"`, and `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` work across all modern browsers. In environments with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, update the text timer at 1-second or 15-second cadence without animated progress rings.

guides.title: Zero-Displacement Agent & Auth Receipts (Choice 1A)
guides.description: Deliver non-blocking agent mutation and step-up authentication receipts in top-layer popover=\"manual\" notes with DeltaY_focal = 0px, opt-in Jump navigation, and inline Undo.
triggers: notifying users after an AI stages or updates an item without scrolling them away
preventing layout shift when showing mutation confirmations or passkey prompts
adding Jump to Workspace and Undo controls to non-blocking receipts
guides.overview: When an operator clicks an action button—staging an AI proposal, applying a tier, or triggering step-up sign-in—automatically scrolling the viewport away or injecting normal-flow banners breaks reading context (`DeltaY_focal != 0`). Keep the camera pinned (`0px` scroll displacement) and project a top-layer `popover="manual"` receipt offering an opt-in `[Jump to Workspace]` button and immediate `[Undo]`.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Decouple state mutation (`ADDRESS` / `MUTATE`) from camera movement (`TRAVERSE`)

Never call `scrollIntoView()` or inject normal-flow confirmation banners above the viewport fold after an action click. Keep `window.scrollY` and the clicked trigger's viewport offset invariant (`DeltaY_focal = 0px`).

### Rule 2: Render receipts in top-layer `popover="manual"` without stealing focus

Use `popover="manual"` so the receipt does not light-dismiss while the operator continues inspecting other items, and never steal focus onto the popover when it opens. Announce the confirmation text via `ariaNotify()` (or a polite `aria-live="polite"` region), pause any auto-hide timer while pointer hover or keyboard focus is inside the popover, and include an explicit `Dismiss` control.

### Rule 3: Provide opt-in Jump and Undo actions only as shortcuts

Every action inside the receipt (`Jump to Workspace` and `Undo`) must mirror controls that already exist durably in the page, ensuring nothing is lost once the popover is dismissed.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** declare `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` as a separate property after `transition` so older browsers still run opacity/transform transitions instead of dropping the entire rule.
- **DO** combine `:popover-open` and `.\:popover-open` inside `:is(...)` so fallback styling works seamlessly.
- **DO** pause the receipt auto-hide timer whenever keyboard focus or pointer hover enters the popover.
- **DO** return focus cleanly to the triggering control if a user manually dismisses a currently focused receipt popover.
- **DON'T** display background receipts while a blocking `<dialog>` modal is open (`showModal()` marks the outside DOM inert).
- **DON'T** steal focus onto `#agent-receipt-popover` when it opens—the user is staying put at their current coordinate.
- **DON'T** put unique irreversible actions solely inside a temporary toast receipt; always keep the same undo/review link durable in the workspace.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Scroll down so `#stage-proposal-btn` is mid-viewport, record `scrollBefore = window.scrollY`, click `#stage-proposal-btn`, and assert `Math.abs(window.scrollY - scrollBefore) === 0` and `document.activeElement === stageBtn`.
  - Assert `#agent-receipt-popover:popover-open` is visible in the top layer and does not increase `document.documentElement.scrollHeight` (`DeltaB_inflow === 0`).
  - Focus `#receipt-undo-btn` and wait > 6s to verify the receipt does not vanish under keyboard focus.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Native Popover (`popover="manual"`) is Baseline Newly Available (2025-01). When `!('popover' in HTMLElement.prototype)`, toggling `hidden = false` and `.\:popover-open` renders the same `position: fixed` bottom-end receipt without external scripts. Use an `aria-live="polite"` node alongside optional `ariaNotify()` so all screen readers announce receipts cleanly.

guides.title: Black-Box Temporal Event Scrubbing & Deterministic Replay
guides.description: Build a 60fps bidirectional temporal playback scrubber spanning historical incident bookmarks, live state, and predictive horizons with zero layout reflow and throttled ARIA narration.
triggers: building a timeline scrubber to replay historical AI or telemetry incidents
jumping directly to incident onset, mitigation, and stabilization bookmarks
preventing layout jitter or screen-reader speech flooding while scrubbing ranges
unifying past event replay, live state, and future projection on one timeline
guides.overview: Interfaces locked to the ephemeral present force operators to guess what sequence of events triggered a fault. A **Multi-Scale Temporal Scrubber** (`MSTS`) pairs a continuous black-box flight recorder with sub-frame seek latency (`<= 16ms`, `60fps`), one-click incident bookmarks, variable-speed playback (`1x`, `5x`, `30x`), and forward predictive horizon exploration—without layout jitter or screen-reader flooding.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Unify past replay, live present (`t=0`), and predictive horizon on one continuous axis

Span negative historical offsets (e.g., `-60m` to `0s`) through `t=0 (LIVE)` into positive predictive projections (`+30m`). Color-code and text-tag the regime badge distinctly (`HISTORICAL REPLAY`, `LIVE STREAMING`, `PREDICTIVE PROJECTION`) so operators never confuse a replayed fault or simulation with live system state.

### Rule 2: Lock seek latency (`<= 16ms`) and guarantee zero horizontal or vertical reflow

Keep frame lookup `O(1)` against an indexed ring buffer of recorded snapshots, coalesce rapid slider `input` events with `requestAnimationFrame`, and apply `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` with fixed `min-inline-size` (`ch` units) on time/value readouts so numbers never cause surrounding controls to jump.

### Rule 3: Provide one-click incident bookmarks and accessible throttled ARIA feedback

Surface key anomaly bookmarks (`Thermal Drift`, `Fault Onset`, `Stabilized`) beside the scrubber for instant jumps (`0` guesswork dragging). Update `aria-valuetext` on every step, but throttle `aria-live="polite"` announcements (`>= 450ms` debounce) so rapid keyboard or pointer scrubbing does not overload screen readers.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** isolate the active timeline mode (`live`, `history`, `future`) with explicit visible text badges as well as color so operators never mistake replay for live control.
- **DO** throttle `aria-live` updates during continuous pointer drags while keeping `aria-valuetext` synchronous on every frame.
- **DO** enforce `tabular-nums` and reserved block/inline sizes (`min-inline-size` in `ch`, `min-block-size` on `.scrub-metrics dd`) so text updates cause `0px` layout shift.
- **DON'T** mutate live state or dispatch commands while scrubbed away from `t=0`; block destructive dispatch unless returning explicitly to `LIVE`.
- **DON'T** animate auto-replay frames rapidly when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active—slow cadence or step explicitly.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
1. **Seek Latency & Reflow Check:** Scrub `#temporal-slider` from `-3600` to `+1800` in Playwright; verify update completes in `< 16ms` and `document.body.scrollHeight` / button `y` coordinates shift by `0px`.
2. **Bookmark Accuracy Check:** Click each `.scrub-bookmark` button and assert `#scrub-mode-badge` switches accurately (`history`, `live`, `future`) and `slider.getAttribute('aria-valuetext')` reflects the new offset.
3. **ARIA Throttle Check:** Dispatch 10 rapid `input` events within 100ms and confirm `#scrub-aria-announcer` emits once after the `450ms` quiet window.

Fallbacks: Standard `<input type="range">` works natively in all browsers with keyboard arrows (<kbd>Left</kbd>/<kbd>Right</kbd>, <kbd>PageUp</kbd>/<kbd>PageDown</kbd>, <kbd>Home</kbd>/<kbd>End</kbd>); if `requestAnimationFrame` coalescing is unnecessary for static logs, invoke `renderFrame` directly.

guides.title: ANSI/ISA-18.2 Cascade Alarm Rationalization
guides.description: Collapse cascading secondary fault floods into prioritized root causes with >=90% suppression ratios so operator attention stays within working-memory limits.
triggers: handling alert storms where one failure triggers dozens of downstream warnings
implementing ANSI/ISA-18.2 alarm flood suppression in AI or telemetry consoles
capping simultaneous top-level alerts inside working-memory limits
keeping suppressed secondary symptoms auditable without cluttering primary view
guides.overview: During a primary system fault, cascading downstream checks often fire 30–50 redundant alarms within seconds. Presenting a flat chronological feed destroys operator situation awareness and induces alarm blindness. Group causal chains dynamically under ANSI/ISA-18.2 principles, suppressing `>= 90%` of symptomatic child alerts into an auditable disclosure while surfacing `<= 4–7` prioritized root causes.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Cluster alerts by causal lineage, not arrival timestamp

Never dump raw telemetry events straight into top-level alert banners. Map each incoming signal to a `rootCauseId` (or causal dependency edge). Promote only the root cause to the primary alert list and move correlated downstream symptoms into a collapsed child group.

### Rule 2: Enforce `>= 90%` cascade suppression during fault floods

Compute `suppressionRatio = suppressedCount / totalRawCount`. During multi-fault cascades (`totalRawCount >= 10`), suppress secondary voltage, heartbeat, or timeout echoes so active root-cause cards stay strictly within working-memory limits (`<= 4` critical chunks; max `7`).

### Rule 3: Preserve lossless auditability inside native `<details>`

Suppression is never deletion. Render a clear suppression badge (`1 Root Cause · 41 Secondary Alarms Suppressed · 97.6%`) paired with a collapsed `<details>` disclosure containing every child timestamp and node ID for post-triage verification.

### Rule 4: Pair color severity with non-color cues and calm live announcements

Indicate priority with both text rank (`P1 CRITICAL`, `P2 WARNING`) and distinct shape/icon glyphs (`aria-hidden="true"`). Route only new unacknowledged root causes—never suppressed child echoes—to `aria-live="assertive"`.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** cap active root-cause cards at `<= 4` (`<= 7` hard ceiling) and display both raw count and suppression percentage transparently.
- **DO** preserve suppressed secondary events in a closed `<details>` disclosure so investigators can audit cascade propagation without blocking immediate remediation.
- **DO** combine priority labels (`P1`, `P2`), icons, and high-contrast borders rather than color-coded dots alone.
- **DON'T** emit every suppressed child alarm into an `aria-live` region; screen-reader speech queues will lag seconds behind live faults.
- **DON'T** delete or drop suppressed child telemetry from logs or audit trails—rationalization suppresses visual attention clutter, not ground-truth history.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
1. **Suppression Ratio Assertion:** Feed 42 synthetic cascade events (1 root + 41 downstream echoes) into `rationalizeAlarms()` and assert `visibleRoots.length === 1` and `suppressionRatio >= 0.90`.
2. **Working-Memory Cap Assertion:** Assert top-level `.alarm-root-card` count in DOM never exceeds `4` at rest and `<details class="alarm-children">` starts collapsed (`!details.open`).
3. **ARIA Flood Check:** Verify `#alarm-live-region` announces `1` concise root-cause string per burst rather than `42` queued messages.

Fallbacks: If causal metadata (`rootCauseId`) is absent on an incoming event stream, fall back to time-window (`<= 5s`) + subsystem deduplication and mark the summary as `[Grouped by Subsystem]` until exact topology edges arrive.

guides.title: Cognitive Ergonomics and Human Factors
guides.description: Apply quantitative biomechanical, attentional, and high-acuity diagnostic ergonomics across AI consoles, operational cockpits, and multi-surface interfaces.
triggers: designing an AI console or operational dashboard for human operators
reducing cognitive load and alarm fatigue in high-acuity workflows
sizing interactive targets, spacing moats, and surface contrast budgets
adapting interfaces across mobile, desktop, vehicle, wearable, and foldable surfaces
guides.overview:
High-consequence AI and operational interfaces fail when they treat the human operator as an unbounded processor with uniform visual acuity, steady hands, and infinite attention. Quantitative cognitive ergonomics (`D28`) enforces measurable biomechanical bounds, working-memory budgets, surface-specific luminance and glance constraints, and crisis-time interface simplification.

Use this discipline to align layout geometry, motion damping, alert triage, predictive forecasting, and temporal playback with real human sensory and motor limits.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
Select the specialized guide that resolves the primary ergonomic bottleneck in your interface:

### Rule 1: Motor precision, choice overload, or visual clutter (`fitts-moat-and-hick-hyman-budgets`)

Apply when users mis-tap adjacent controls, hesitate over oversized toolbars, or confront dense walls of cards and nested borders. Enforce pointer-variance collision moats (`d_moat`), `>= 44x44px` touch / `>= 48x48px` emergency targets, Miller/Halford `<= 4–7` chunks, `W_density` in `[0.22, 0.45]`, and single-beacon viewport arbitration.

### Rule 2: Physical form factor or harsh lighting mismatch (`environmental-surface-archetypes`)

Apply when the same UI runs across outdoor sunlight mobile, desktop studios, vehicle consoles, wearables, or dual-screen foldables. Enforce `>= 7:1` outdoor contrast, `<= 14`-word / `300ms` glance budgets, thumb-zone escapes, and `viewport-segments` fold avoidance.

### Rule 3: Retrospective telemetry hiding future risk (`endsley-predictive-horizon-projection`)

Apply when dashboards only report past or current state (Endsley Levels 1–2). Upgrade to explicit `t+5m`, `t+15m`, and `t+30m` trajectory horizons with calibrated confidence intervals, pre-execution What-If blast-radius sandboxes, and dual-signatory shift handovers.

### Rule 4: Secondary alert storms drowning root causes (`cascade-alarm-rationalization`)

Apply when a single upstream fault triggers dozens of downstream warnings. Enforce ANSI/ISA-18.2 cascade suppression (`>= 90%` alarm reduction) to collapse secondary floods into prioritized root causes within working-memory limits.

### Rule 5: Acute crisis or operator tunnel vision (`stress-adaptive-battlestation-mode`)

Apply when operators must stabilize a live anomaly under physiological stress. Provide an instant Battle-Station mode that dims or marks peripheral panels `inert`, caps active chunks at `<= 3`, expands actuators to `>= 48px`, and boosts chromatic contrast.

### Rule 6: Post-incident diagnosis or trajectory verification (`blackbox-temporal-event-scrubbing`)

Apply when operators need to trace what preceded a fault or project forward momentum. Render a `60fps` (`<= 16ms` seek) bidirectional scrubber spanning historical black-box frames, live telemetry, and predictive projections without layout reflow.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** bind interactive target sizes (`--ergo-target-min`) and inter-control collision moats (`--ergo-d-moat`) to real pointer precision (`@media (pointer: coarse)` vs fine desktop).
- **DO** enforce strict resting density equilibrium (`W_density` in `[0.22, 0.45]`, `<= 4–7` working-memory chunks per view) so critical signals stand out without visual congestion.
- **DO** isolate emergency or primary actions with a single `TIER_1_GOAL_BEACON` per viewport rather than rendering competing solid-fill primary buttons.
- **DON'T** rely on raw past/current metrics alone in high-risk interfaces; pair them with forward projection horizons (`t+5m`, `t+15m`, `t+30m`) and uncertainty intervals.
- **DON'T** dump ungrouped secondary alarms or hover-only tooltips onto operational views; rationalize cascades and keep every critical actuator keyboard-reachable.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
Run automated DOM geometry checks at both desktop (`1440x900`, fine pointer) and mobile (`390x844`, coarse pointer):

1. **Target & Moat Audit:** Assert `rect.width >= 44 && rect.height >= 44` for every interactive button/control when `(pointer: coarse)` is emulated, and assert minimum edge-to-edge separation `>= d_moat` (`8px` mobile, `4px` desktop) between sibling hitboxes.
2. **Single-Beacon Audit:** Assert `document.querySelectorAll('[data-ui-ir-focus-tier="TIER_1_GOAL_BEACON"]')` intersecting the viewport has length `<= 1` across scroll stops (`0%` to `100%` scroll height).
3. **Zero Overflow:** Assert `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= document.documentElement.clientWidth` at `320px`, `390px`, and `1440px`.

Fallbacks: When `@media (pointer: coarse)` is unsupported or hybrid touch-laptops switch input modes, default emergency/dispatch actuators to `>= 44px` via `min-block-size` and expand via padding rather than fixed heights so OS font scaling never clips labels.

guides.title: Endsley Level 3 Predictive Horizon Projection & Consequence Sandboxes
guides.description: Upgrade AI and operational consoles from retrospective Level 1-2 telemetry to Endsley Level 3 trajectory horizons (t+5m, t+15m, t+30m) with uncertainty bounds and pre-execution What-If blast-radius simulation.
triggers: building an AI forecasting or operational telemetry dashboard
preventing retrospective dashboards from hiding upcoming failures or resource exhaustion
simulating blast radius and life-safety protection before an irreversible dispatch action
designing crew shift handover summaries that preserve future trajectory awareness
guides.overview: Dashboards that report only raw current telemetry (Endsley Level 1 Perception) and status summaries (Level 2 Comprehension) force operators to run error-prone mental simulations to guess what breaks next. Upgrade high-acuity AI consoles to **Endsley Level 3 (Projection)**: explicit forward horizons at `t+5m`, `t+15m`, and `t+30m` paired with calibrated uncertainty bounds, pre-execution What-If consequence sandboxes, and verifiable crew handovers.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Render three explicit time-horizon checkpoints (`t+5m`, `t+15m`, `t+30m`)

Never show a bare sparkline or single-point forecast without temporal anchors and risk intervals:

- Always display **three discrete projection horizons** (`t+5m`, `t+15m`, `t+30m`) alongside estimated time-to-depletion (`t_depletion`) and cascade risk probability (`P_cascade`).
- Pair every projected metric with an explicit **confidence interval or uncertainty band** (e.g., `95% CI: 59.88–59.98 Hz`) that widens cleanly over longer horizons so operators never confuse a forecast with measured ground truth.

### Rule 2: Gate high-impact interventions with a What-If consequence sandbox

Before committing destructive or load-affecting actions (such as load shedding, rate throttling, or circuit isolation), provide a live simulation slider/input (`#slider-what-if`) calculating downstream impact and explicitly certifying protected life-safety facilities (e.g., `Ward A: 100% Protected`) with zero live side effects during simulation.

### Rule 3: Preserve predictive awareness across crew shift handovers

Compile active projections, open warnings, and simulated mitigations into a structured handover dossier requiring explicit outgoing and incoming operator acknowledgement before transfer closes.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** present `t+5m`, `t+15m`, and `t+30m` projections using `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so streaming numeric updates never jitter horizontally.
- **DO** show wider uncertainty margins at `t+30m` than `t+5m` to communicate forecast decay honestly.
- **DO** isolate What-If simulation controls from live dispatch execution—sliding a parameter must preview consequences without dispatching side effects.
- **DON'T** display model projections as deterministic point values without confidence bounds or horizon timestamps.
- **DON'T** allow shift handovers to close silently when projected risks (`t_depletion < 60m` or `P_cascade >= 0.05`) are unresolved; require explicit dual sign-off.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
1. **Horizon Presence Check:** Assert DOM contains distinct `t+5m`, `t+15m`, and `t+30m` headers/rows with non-empty numeric uncertainty intervals (`±` or `[low, high]`).
2. **Sandbox Isolation Check:** Sweep `#sa-shed-slider` across `0 -> 50` in Playwright and assert `#sa-blast-readout` updates live (`textContent` changes) while issuing `0` mutating network `POST` requests.
3. **Tabular Numeric Stability:** Verify `getBoundingClientRect().width` of table columns changes by `0px` across forecast updates.

Fallbacks: When live WebSocket/SSE telemetry drops, freeze the last verified projection timestamp, mark the horizon header `[STALE · LAST SYNC <time>]`, and prevent blind reliance on stale extrapolated curves.

guides.title: Environmental Surface Archetypes & Foldable Viewport Segments
guides.description: Adapt luminance contrast (>=7:1), glance word budgets (<=14 words / 300ms), touch targets, and viewport-segment grids across handheld outdoor, desktop studio, mounted vehicle, wearable, and foldable surfaces.
triggers: designing mobile interfaces used outdoors in high glare or direct sunlight
building in-vehicle consoles, wrist wearables, or field-mounted displays
preventing content and controls from splitting across a foldable device hinge
setting glance word budgets and thumb-zone abort actions by hardware posture
guides.overview: Treating every viewport as a generic responsive breakpoint (`@media (min-width: 768px)`) ignores physical glare, motion vibration, thumb reach, and dual-screen hinges. A pedestrian reading outdoors under glare cannot parse a low-contrast multi-column table, and an operator on a foldable tablet cannot tap a button straddling the physical hinge crease. Bind rendering to explicit physical surface archetypes (`surface.schema.json`) and foldable viewport segments.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
Apply the rules matching the target hardware and physical environment:

| Archetype | Contrast Floor | Target Floor | Glance & Decision Budget | Structural Rule |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `HANDHELD_OUTDOOR_HIGH_LUMINANCE` | `>= 7:1` (AAA) | `>= 44x44px` | `<= 14` words / `300ms`; `<= 3.0s` digest | Bottom thumb-zone primary + `1-tap` abort; `safe-area-inset-*` |
| `DESKTOP_OPERATOR_STUDIO` | `>= 4.5:1` (AA) | `>= 24x24px` (`28px` ideal) | Multi-column `60–75ch` measure | Keyboard shortcuts + multi-pane preview inspectors |
| `MOUNTED_OPERATIONAL_CONSOLE` | `>= 7:1` | `>= 48–56px` | Immediate peripheral readability | Zero hover-only UI; oversized step controls for vibration |
| `EMBEDDED_MINIATURE_WEARABLE` | `>= 7:1` | `>= 48px` | `1` status chip + `1` abort/ack action | Suppress multi-row prose and nested scrolling |
| `FOLDABLE_DUAL_SCREEN` | Surface-matched | `>= 44px` | Split left/right logical panes | Align columns to `viewport-segment-width`; never span hinge |

### Rule 1: Enforce outdoor luminance and glance ceilings

When operating outdoors or in motion (`HANDHELD_OUTDOOR_HIGH_LUMINANCE`, `MOUNTED_OPERATIONAL_CONSOLE`), clamp primary status chips to `<= 14` words (`300ms` peripheral glance budget) and elevate text/surface contrast to `>= 7:1` rather than translucent muted grays.

### Rule 2: Keep primary and abort controls inside the thumb zone

On handheld and mounted surfaces, anchor primary progression and `1-tap` hard-abort actions to the bottom reach zone padded by `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` and pair `scroll-padding-bottom` so focused elements are never obscured by fixed bars (WCAG 2.4.11).

### Rule 3: Respect physical folds with `viewport-segments`

On dual-screen or foldable devices (`(horizontal-viewport-segments: 2)` or `(vertical-viewport-segments: 2)`), map layout grids explicitly to the physical segment boundary using `env(viewport-segment-width 0 0)` and `env(viewport-segment-left 1 0)` so dialogs, charts, and primary buttons never cross the fold hinge.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** enforce `>= 7:1` contrast (solid high-contrast ink/canvas tokens) for outdoor handheld, vehicle-mounted, and wearable surfaces—avoid semi-transparent frosted glass over busy backgrounds.
- **DO** cap Tier-1 glance chips at `<= 14` words (`<= 6` words on wearables) and pad fixed bars with `env(safe-area-inset-*)`.
- **DO** bind dual-pane layouts to `@media (horizontal-viewport-segments: 2)` and `env(viewport-segment-width 0 0)` so controls stay cleanly inside one physical display segment.
- **DON'T** require hover (`:hover`) to reveal labels or status explanations on touch, mounted, or foldable surfaces.
- **DON'T** use `scroll-padding-bottom: 0` when rendering bottom thumb-zone bars; keyboard focus must stay unobscured.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
1. **Contrast & Target Verification:** Audit computed foreground/background contrast (`>= 7.0:1` for outdoor/mounted/wearable, `>= 4.5:1` desktop) and target boxes (`>= 44x44px` coarse, `>= 48px` mounted/wearable).
2. **Foldable Segment Check:** Emulate dual-segment posture (`width: 1114px` or `horizontal-viewport-segments: 2`) in Playwright and verify primary buttons sit strictly left or right of the hinge offset (`x + width <= left_segment_width || x >= right_segment_left`).
3. **Glance Budget Check:** Assert `.surface-glance-chip` word count `<= 14` on mobile/outdoor postures.

Fallbacks: Standard single-screen browsers ignore `@media (horizontal-viewport-segments: 2)` and `env(viewport-segment-*)` and fall back to the single-column `1fr` / `auto-fit` grid cleanly; add a `@media (min-width: 900px)` two-column layout if desktop side-by-side panes are also desired.

guides.title: Fitts's Moat, Hick-Hyman Choice Caps & Single-Beacon Arbitration
guides.description: Size interactive targets and pointer-variance collision moats, cap working-memory choice cardinality, maintain resting whitespace equilibrium, and arbitrate a single primary beacon per viewport.
triggers: preventing accidental mis-clicks or fat-finger errors between adjacent buttons
choosing between toggle, segmented control, popover menu, or combobox by item count
reducing dense UI clutter into 4-7 working-memory chunks and balanced whitespace
fixing competing primary CTA buttons across a single viewport
guides.overview: Adjacent buttons cause accidental clicks when spacing ignores pointer positional variance (`sigma_p`), and dense toolbars stall operator decisions when visible options exceed human working-memory limits (`C_WM <= 4–7` chunks). Combining Fitts's Law moats (`d_moat`), Hick-Hyman morphology thresholds, balanced resting density (`W_density` in `[0.22, 0.45]`), and strict single-beacon arbitration eliminates motor slips and visual competition simultaneously.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Scale hitboxes and collision moats (`d_moat`) to pointer variance

Derive target dimensions and spacing from Fitts's Index of Difficulty (`ID = log2(2D / W_eff)`) and pointer variance (`d_moat >= k * sigma_p`):

- **Coarse Touch (`pointer: coarse`):** Minimum `44x44px` hitbox (`48x48px` for primary/emergency actions), `8–12px` collision moat (`d_moat`), and `16px` outer screen-edge bleed.
- **Fine Desktop (`pointer: fine`):** Minimum `24x24px` (`26–28px` recommended), `4–6px` collision moat (`d_moat`), and `24–40px` macro-gutters.
- **Emergency / High-Stress Actuators:** Minimum `48x48px` regardless of pointer type, with `>= 12px` moat from any destructive sibling control.
- **Topological Spacing Hierarchy:** Keep intra-entity gaps smaller than inter-tuple gaps and inter-operator moats (`d_1 < d_2 < d_3`, e.g., `6px < 14px < 28px`).

### Rule 2: Clamp spring overshoot against the collision moat

Never allow animated transitions to swing an element into a neighbor's moat during flight. Enforce peak excursion `A_overshoot <= 0.5 * d_moat`. If an underdamped elastic spring (`zeta < 1.0`) produces `deltaX * exp(-pi * zeta / sqrt(1 - zeta^2)) > 0.5 * d_moat`, automatically clamp damping to `zeta >= 1.0` (critically damped, zero overshoot).

### Rule 3: Select control morphology by Hick-Hyman cardinality (`N`)

Hick-Hyman decision latency grows logarithmically with options (`H = log2(N + 1)`). Route option sets deterministically by cardinality `N` and cap working-memory chunks at `C_WM <= 4` propositions per band (`<= 7` max) and `<= 24` characters per wayfinding chip:

- `N = 2`: Binary toggle switch, checkbox, or two-option `<fieldset>` radio pair.
- `2 < N <= 5`: Inline segmented control or radio group (`<= 1` unclipped row on desktop).
- `6 <= N <= 20`: Collapsed native `[popover]` menu or `<select>`.
- `N > 20`: Searchable filterable combobox or Choice 2B floating match window.

### Rule 4: Maintain resting density equilibrium and single-beacon salience

Keep resting surface ink density `W_density` within `[0.22, 0.45]` (interstitial openness `W_interstitial >= 0.55`) and nested border depth `D_nest <= 2` (avoid card-inside-card-inside-card boxing). Crown at most ONE active `TIER_1_GOAL_BEACON` across any active viewport window; demote off-focus section CTAs to `TIER_2_STANDBY_SECTION_BEACON` (outlined accent) and peripheral utilities to `TIER_4_AMBIENT_UTILITY`.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** wrap radio/checkbox labels around their `<input>` and size the `<label>` to `--ergo-hitbox` (`>= 44px` on coarse touch) so the entire control meets Fitts's floor.
- **DO** cap resting propositions per band at `<= 4` (`<= 7` max), chip labels at `<= 24` chars, and nested borders at `D_nest <= 2`.
- **DO** enforce `>= 12px` edge-to-edge gap between positive confirmation actuators and destructive (`Discard`, `Delete`) buttons.
- **DON'T** render two solid-fill `TIER_1_GOAL_BEACON` buttons simultaneously inside the same viewport; demote non-focal section actions to `TIER_2_STANDBY_SECTION_BEACON`.
- **DON'T** apply bouncy underdamped springs (`zeta < 1`) to controls whose peak overshoot exceeds `0.5 * d_moat`.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
1. **Hitbox & Moat Check (Playwright):** Emulate `{ hasTouch: true }` and assert every interactive target satisfies `box.width >= 44 && box.height >= 44` (`>= 48` for emergency/primary actuators) and `auditCollisionMoat(root, 8).length === 0`.
2. **Density & Chunk Check:** Verify section whitespace openness `>= 0.55` (`W_density` in `[0.22, 0.45]`), visible propositions per sub-band `<= 4`, and nested bordered container depth `<= 2`.
3. **Single-Beacon Check:** Verify `document.querySelectorAll('[data-ui-ir-focus-tier="TIER_1_GOAL_BEACON"]')` in viewport is `<= 1`.

Fallbacks: When `:has(input:checked)` is unavailable on legacy engines, bind a lightweight `change` listener toggling `.is-selected` on the parent `.ergo-seg-option`; CSS `gap` and `min-block-size` already guarantee Fitts moats cleanly everywhere.

guides.title: Stress-Adaptive Battle-Station Mode
guides.description: Simplify operational interfaces under acute crises by marking peripheral chrome inert, capping active chunks at <=3, expanding actuators to >=48px, and elevating contrast to counter tunnel vision.
triggers: designing an emergency or crisis override mode for high-stress operator tasks
preventing tunnel vision and tremor mis-taps during critical system faults
suppressing non-essential analytics and dashboards while preserving safe abort controls
making critical emergency buttons >=48px with high contrast and keyboard isolation
guides.overview: Under acute operational crises, human operators suffer perceptual narrowing (tunnel vision), degraded fine motor steadiness, and working-memory collapse. Leaving full analytical chrome, decorative metrics, and small `28px` buttons on screen slows triage and raises mis-click risk. Provide an explicit **Battle-Station Mode** that isolates `<= 3` critical decision chunks, marks non-essential regions `inert`, expands actuators to `>= 48x48px`, and boosts contrast cleanly.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Suppress peripheral regions cleanly with `inert` and dimmed styling

Visual dimming (`opacity: 0.25`) alone leaves hidden/dimmed buttons reachable via keyboard <kbd>Tab</kbd> and screen readers. When Battle-Station mode engages, mark every non-critical sibling region `inert` alongside visual dimming so focus moves strictly between the critical fault readout and safe emergency actuators.

### Rule 2: Cap active chunks at `<= 3` and expand actuators to `>= 48x48px`

Limit visible primary focal blocks inside Battle-Station mode to `<= 3` critical items (root fault summary, stabilization actuator, and safe exit/undo). Expand all active actuators to `min-block-size: 48px; min-inline-size: 48px` (`12px+` collision moat) and `>= 1rem` typography.

### Rule 3: Elevate contrast without destructive color-only ambiguity

Switch to a high-contrast dark obsidian or light high-contrast palette (`>= 7:1` text contrast, `>= 1.85` focal border salience ratio) and respect `@media (forced-colors: active)` and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Never obscure the toggle needed to exit Battle-Station mode.

### Rule 4: Require deliberate toggle or reversible confirmation

Never swap layouts unexpectedly mid-pointer-hover without clear status announcement (`aria-live="assertive"`). Keep the mode reversible in one tap (`Disengage Battle-Station`) so operators retain full control.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** set `element.inert = true` on suppressed peripheral panels so keyboard users and screen readers stay inside the critical cockpit.
- **DO** expand every critical actuator and exit toggle to `>= 48x48px` with `>= 12px` spacing and `1rem+` text.
- **DO** cap focal items inside the crisis panel at `<= 3` chunks (Fault, Action 1, Safe Alternative/Exit).
- **DON'T** move the toggle button under the cursor when Battle-Station activates (`0px` displacement of `#btn-toggle-battlestation` or clear opt-out label).
- **DON'T** trap the user with `pointer-events: none` on the disengage control or hide status feedback from assistive tech.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
1. **Inert & Focus Check:** Engage Battle-Station in Playwright and verify `panel.inert === true` on all `[data-peripheral-chrome="true"]` containers and that pressing <kbd>Tab</kbd> never focuses a peripheral link or button.
2. **Actuator Geometry Check:** Assert every visible `.ergo-control` has `box.width >= 48 && box.height >= 48` when `[data-ergo-mode="battlestation"]` is active.
3. **Chunk & Contrast Check:** Verify visible foreground/background contrast `>= 7:1` inside `.ops-panel--critical` and `<= 3` critical chunks rendered.

Fallbacks: `HTMLElement.prototype.inert` is Baseline Widely Available (since 2023). On ultra-legacy browsers without `inert`, pair `aria-hidden="true"` with storing/restoring `tabindex="-1"` on descendant focusables inside peripheral panels.

guides.title: Anti-Cliche Lexical Hygiene & Sentence Ceilings
guides.description: Eliminate generic AI/SaaS marketing fluff, enforce <=14-18 word sentence ceilings, cap Jargon De-Escalation Index <=0.05, and expand necessary domain acronyms on first visual scan.
triggers: auditing AI-generated UI copy for generic SaaS buzzwords
enforcing readable word ceilings on buttons, cards, and headings

guides.overview: AI-generated interfaces routinely pad empty substance with hollow marketing adjectives ("seamless", "magic", "revolutionary", "supercharge") and sprawling multi-clause sentences. # Dual-Habitat Jargon Quarantine & Homograph-Safe Linting

## Overview

End-user screens lose trust and comprehension when they surface backend acronyms like `SHA-256`, `RLS`, `Cedar`, `SCIM`, `JWT`, `FSM`, `JSONB`, `WORM`, or `UI-IR`. Transduce each mechanism into its everyday human North Star on Habitat A, route verifiable receipts to Habitat B (`/_observatory`), and lint copy with homograph-safe rules so legitimate words like "earthworm", "Cedar Street", or "church spire" never trigger false positives.

## Decision Rules

### Rule 1: Transduce every backend primitive into its human North Star on Habitat A

Never display raw database, auth, or compiler vocabulary on consumer or frontline surfaces. Map each mechanism to what it protects for the person using the interface:

| Submerged Plumbing Token | Habitat A Human North Star | Habitat B (`/_observatory`) Proof |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `SHA-256` / `WORM` | "Tamper-proof activity record" | Ed25519 + Merkle chain height & root digest |
| `RLS` | "Visible only inside your workspace" | Tenant-scoped PostgreSQL `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` proof |
| `Cedar` / `OpenFGA` | "Checked against your team's safety rules" | Policy decision log & authorization rule ID |
| `SCIM` / `JWT` | "Verified teammate session" | Token issuer, `act` claim, and directory sync trace |
| `FSM` / `JSONB` | "Predictable step-by-step progress" | State machine transition ledger & snapshot schema |
| `UI-IR` / `@steer:` | *Completely submerged (zero frontstage output)* | Compiler discipline provenance manifest |

### Rule 2: Enforce homograph-safe matching in static copy linters

Naive substring or case-insensitive word matching produces false alarms on legitimate domain terms (`canine worm`, `heartworm`, `Pacific red cedar`, `Cedar Street`, `church spire`). Restrict ambiguous tokens (`worm`, `cedar`, `spire`) to uppercase acronyms (`/\bWORM\b/`, `/\bSPIRE\b/`) or technical collocations (`worm audit`, `Cedar policy`, `SPIFFE/SPIRE`).

### Rule 3: Exclude quarantined Habitat B slots before Habitat A verification

Ignore `<script>`, `<style>`, `<svg>`, `<template>`, `[hidden]`, and `[data-meta-quarantined="true"]` elements when extracting Habitat A visible text, while keeping Habitat B panels strictly separate under `/_observatory`.

## Implementation Pattern

```js
// Homograph-safe Habitat A jargon validator (zero dependencies).
const UNCONDITIONAL_PLUMBING = [
  'scim', 'sdek', 'rls', 'oscal', 'etag', 'spiffe', 'odata', 'opencost',
  'pkcs11', 'ml-dsa', 'clickhouse', 'debezium', 'zarf', 'tetragon', 'ebpf',
  'oidc', 'saml', 'jwt', 'jsonb', 'fsm', 'postgres', 'postgresql', 'sha-256',
  'ui-ir', 'cryptoshred'
];

function isAmbiguousPlumbingLeak(token, text) {
  if (token === 'worm') {
    return /\bWORM\b/.test(text) ||
      /\bworm[\s_-]+(?:audit|ledger|storage|retention|compliance|log|rules?|immutable)\b/i.test(text) ||
      /\bwrite[- ]once[- ]read[- ]many\b/i.test(text);
  }
  if (token === 'cedar') {
    return /\bCedar\s+(?:policy|policies|ABAC|RBAC|PDP|engine|schema|guard|rules?)\b/i.test(text) ||
      /\bAWS\s+Cedar\b/i.test(text);
  }
  if (token === 'spire') {
    return /\bSPIRE\b/.test(text) ||
      /\bSPIFFE\s*[/&-]\s*SPIRE\b/i.test(text) ||
      /\bspire[\s_-]+(?:agent|server|workload|svid)\b/i.test(text);
  }
  return false;
}

export function lintHabitatACopy(visibleText) {
  const leaks = [];
  for (const token of UNCONDITIONAL_PLUMBING) {
    const escaped = token.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
    if (new RegExp(`\\b${escaped}\\b`, 'i').test(visibleText)) {
      leaks.push(token);
    }
  }
  for (const homograph of ['worm', 'cedar', 'spire']) {
    if (isAmbiguousPlumbingLeak(homograph, visibleText)) {
      leaks.push(homograph);
    }
  }
  return { passed: leaks.length === 0, leaks };
}
```

## Guidelines

- **DO** verify copy against both unconditional plumbing tokens and homograph-safe contextual regexes before publishing Habitat A copy.
- **DO** inspect actual rendered DOM text (`document.body.innerText` on visible nodes) as well as source templates, because dynamic error handlers often leak raw server codes (`ETag mismatch`, `RLS violation`) into alerts.
- **DO** keep an explicit human translation table for every compliance and security guarantee surfaced in product copy.
- **DON'T** block legitimate veterinary, botanical, or geographic domain copy (`earthworm`, `Cedar St`, `cathedral spire`) with brittle substring blacklists.
- **DON'T** mark visible Habitat A marketing copy with `data-meta-quarantined="true"` to evade the linter; only genuine hidden or `/_observatory` blocks belong behind quarantine.
- **DON'T** show raw `0x...` hex hashes or state enum strings (`TRANSIT_INSPECTION`) inside primary action cards.

## Verification & Fallbacks

- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Run `lintHabitatACopy(visibleText)` on every Habitat A route (`/` and primary user flows) and assert `passed === true` (`leaks.length === 0`).
  - Run unit assertions confirming `"Prevent heartworm on Cedar Street"` passes (`leaks.length === 0`) while `"Protected by WORM audit and Cedar policy"` fails (`leaks` includes `'worm'` and `'cedar'`).
  - Navigate to `/_observatory` (Habitat B) and assert technical receipts render intact without breaking Habitat A isolation.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Pure standard regular expressions and DOM node filtering work identically across all JavaScript runtimes (Node >= 22 and every browser).

**DON'T** replace missing domain substance with marketing clichés ("seamless", "magic", "revolutionary", "next-gen"). - **DON'T** force users into Habitat B (`/observatory.html`) just to complete everyday tasks or undo a mistake. ## Verification & Fallbacks - **DOM & Playwright assertions:** - Extract visible text from all Habitat A views (`extractVisibleHabitatAText(document.body)`) and assert `0` banned plumbing tokens (`RLS`, `Cedar`, `SCIM`, `JWT`, `WORM`, `JSONB`, `SHA-256`, `OSCAL`, `SPIFFE`) and `maxWordsPerSentence <= 18`. - Verify the Habitat B link (`a[href="/_observatory"]`) resolves cleanly (HTTP `200`) when institutional audit access is enabled, or is cleanly gated in non-auditor builds without dead `href="#"` stubs. -
