guides.title: Imperative Affordance Grammar for Action Controls
guides.description: Write unambiguous buttons and action controls following the [Active Imperative Verb] + [Direct Object] + [Risk/Reversibility Scope] syntax, eliminating vague Submit or OK labels.
triggers: writing labels for AI action buttons, confirmations, or destructive controls
replacing vague Submit, Confirm, Proceed, or OK buttons
communicating reversibility and cost directly inside interactive controls
guides.overview: Generic button labels like `Submit`, `OK`, `Execute`, or `Confirm` force operators to guess what entity will change and whether the change can be undone. Format every mutating or supervisory control using **`[Active Imperative Verb] + [Direct Object] + [Risk / Reversibility Scope]`** so users know the exact consequence before clicking.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Construct every action label from three explicit parts

Follow the exact syntactic structure on buttons, menu commands, and modal triggers:
- **Active Imperative Verb:** `Stage`, `Apply`, `Hold`, `Pull`, `Pause`, `Decommission`, `Restore`, `Send` (never passive voice or bare `Submit` / `Click here`).
- **Direct Object:** Concrete domain entity (`Batch #418`, `Feeder Cap`, `Draft Reply`, `Care Plan`).
- **Risk / Reversibility Scope:** Explicit cost or recovery envelope in a compact subordinate cue (`1-Tap Undo`, `0 Penalty`, `Reversible 15m`, `Irreversible` or `Permanent`).

### Rule 2: Differentiate low-risk staging from irreversible commitment

Keep reversible staging labels calm and reassuring (`Stage Schedule Change (Reversible 15m)`), while marking permanent actions unambiguously (`Permanently Delete Draft (Cannot Undo)`). Keep button copy concise (`<= 8` words) so controls never wrap awkwardly or overflow `390px` containers.

### Rule 3: Preserve accessible-name congruence

Ensure the visible button text matches the accessible name announced by screen readers (`textContent`), rather than overriding an unclear icon or generic `Go` label solely with `aria-label`.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** start every action label with a clear active verb and name the exact affected entity.
- **DO** include the risk or reversibility boundary directly inside the control or its immediate `<dialog>` pair (`(Reversible 15m)`, `(0 Fee)`, `(Permanent)`).
- **DO** put `autofocus` on the safe retention option (`Keep Unit Active`) in destructive dialogs so accidental `Enter` presses never destroy state.
- **DON'T** ship standalone `Submit`, `OK`, `Yes`, `Proceed`, or `Delete` buttons without object and risk context.
- **DON'T** stuff full multi-sentence explanations (`> 10` words) inside a button; keep buttons concise and place extended rules above the button row.
- **DON'T** override a visible `Save` button with a different hidden `aria-label` (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name).
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Run `lintButtonAffordances(document)` on active views and assert `violations.length === 0`.
  - Verify every button inside `.affordance-row` renders both verb+object and risk scope visibly without ellipsis clipping at `390px` viewport width and passes `min-block-size >= 44px`.
  - Open `#purge-confirm-dialog` and assert `document.activeElement.value === 'cancel'`.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Native `<button>` controls with nested `<span>` text render one unified accessible name across all browsers and assistive technologies. Add a `showModal()` click fallback when `!('commandForElement' in HTMLButtonElement.prototype)`.

guides.title: Micro-Atomic Lifecycle Narration for CRUD & Rehydration
guides.description: Transform opaque CRUD and session hydration mechanics into causal lifecycle narratives: Inception (Create), Observability Calibration (Read), Causal Metamorphosis (Update), and Capacity-Releasing Decommissioning (Delete).
triggers: narrating create, filter, update, delete, and restore events in AI workspaces
explaining session startup and cached state recovery clearly to operators
replacing generic Deleted or Updated toasts with causal resource deltas
guides.overview: Even well-designed workflows collapse into lifeless utility chrome when Create, Read, Update, Delete, and page reload emit generic messages like `Record saved` or `Item deleted`. Bind every atomic mutation and session startup event to a clear causal narrative explaining what capacity changed, what threshold triggered, and what safeguard sealed the step.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Narrate all four CRUD operations as causal domain events

Map every atomic state mutation to concrete cause and measurable effect:
- **Create (Inception Event):** State the newly provisioned capacity or scope and initial safety posture (`Staged Substation Plan #12 · 150 kW allocated inside 15m safety window`).
- **Read / Filter (Observability Calibration):** Summarize what risk or slice horizon is now in view (`Showing 4 active schedules exceeding 80% load threshold`).
- **Update (Causal Metamorphosis):** State the state transition, threshold crossed, and net numeric delta (`Shifted from Simulating to Active Hold: -40 kW net peak reduction`).
- **Delete (Capacity-Releasing Decommissioning):** Report released capacity, resource return, and tombstone reference (`Decommissioned Unit #09: returned 45 kW to pool · receipt #tmb-82c1`).

### Rule 2: Distinguish Fresh Inception from Rehydrated Provenance at startup

Never restore saved client state silently in `loadState()`. Surface a quiet single-line session status note distinguishing **Fresh Baseline Calibration** (new clean session) from **Restored Verified Session** (resuming existing staged plans and intact audit continuity).

### Rule 3: Keep lifecycle narration concise and accessible

Keep every narrated event `<= 18` words on Habitat A, update a single polite status region (`role="status"`), and never inject raw internal enum keys (`STORE_UPSERT`, `TOMBSTONED`) into visible user text.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** include concrete deltas (`+45 kW`, `-15 kW`, `3 units matching`) in every lifecycle status announcement.
- **DO** tell the operator on load whether they started fresh or resumed prior saved work without silent surprises.
- **DO** construct narrative DOM entries using `document.createElement` and `textContent`, never string-interpolated `innerHTML`.
- **DON'T** emit generic `Item updated` or `Success` messages with zero causal context.
- **DON'T** expose raw internal event names (`EXT_BUCKET_KEY_SET`, `STORE_UPSERT`, `PAYLOAD_HYDRATION`) in Habitat A activity logs.
- **DON'T** mutate `localStorage` without guarding against private-mode quota exceptions.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Load with empty `localStorage` and assert `#session-narrative-ticker` announces fresh baseline calibration; trigger Create, reload the page, and assert `#session-narrative-ticker` reports restored session state.
  - Trigger Create, Calibrate, Update, and Decommission in sequence and assert `#narrative-audit-feed` prepends causal delta entries (`<= 18` words each) with zero raw enum leakage.
- **Browser fallbacks:** Wrap `localStorage` access in `try/catch` so strict privacy modes degrade cleanly to in-memory session state without throwing runtime errors.

guides.title: Reading-Cadence AI Streaming & Safe Interruption
guides.description: Throttle streamed AI text to 250-400 WPM (20-25ms character cadence) with zero layout shift, an immediate Reveal All shortcut, and an instant AbortController Stop control.
triggers: streaming LLM responses progressively in the UI
preventing layout shift or unreadable token bursts during AI generation
adding Stop and Reveal All controls to streaming AI output
guides.overview: Unthrottled LLM token bursts flash text faster than human eyes can track and push surrounding buttons down the page as lines wrap. Smooth progressive disclosure to human reading speed (`250–400 WPM`, roughly `20–25ms` per 2-character reveal), pin controls above a fixed-footprint output surface (`CLS = 0`), and keep both `Reveal All` and `Stop` immediately clickable.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Throttle token reveal to `250–400 WPM` with `prefers-reduced-motion` bypass

Buffer incoming network chunks and emit characters at `20–25ms` intervals (~`280 WPM` average) so operators read smoothly without erratic token stalls. When `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` matches or the user clicks `Reveal All`, flush the buffered response at once without character-by-character animation.

### Rule 2: Lock control positions above the stream container (`CLS = 0`)

Place `Reveal All` and `Stop` controls in a header row *above* the streaming output box—never below it where growing text pushes buttons away from the user's pointer. Reserve a stable minimum height (`min-block-size`) and `scrollbar-gutter: stable` on the scrollable output container.

### Rule 3: Provide an `AbortController` Stop handle and safe live-region semantics

Wire `Stop Generating` directly to `AbortController.abort()` so network streaming and local timers halt in `< 50ms`. Keep the output container present in the DOM from load with `aria-live="polite"`, set `aria-busy="true"` while tokens stream (preventing screen readers from reading half-words aloud), clear `aria-busy="false"` on completion or abort, and append text strictly via `textContent`—never `innerHTML`.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** place `Reveal All` and `Stop` in a stable toolbar above `#stream-output` so controls never drift beneath growing text.
- **DO** assign streamed tokens exclusively via `textContent` or `append(textNode)` to block prompt-injected HTML or XSS execution.
- **DO** set `aria-busy="true"` while tokens stream and clear it to `"false"` on finish, `Reveal All`, or `Stop`.
- **DO** inspect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and skip character-by-character animation automatically when reduced motion is enabled.
- **DON'T** use `innerHTML += chunk` while streaming model output.
- **DON'T** move keyboard focus inside `#stream-output` during streaming.
- **DON'T** let rapid token updates resize surrounding layout columns (`scrollbar-gutter: stable` + bounded `max-block-size` prevent horizontal jitter).
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Start streaming and record `btnStop.getBoundingClientRect().top` at `t=50ms` and `t=400ms`; assert `0px` vertical button shift while text populates `#stream-output`.
  - Verify `outputEl.getAttribute('aria-busy') === 'true'` during active streaming and `'false'` after clicking `Reveal All` or `Stop`.
  - Under emulated `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, click `#btn-stream-start` and assert complete text appears synchronously without `22ms` timer animation.
- **Browser fallbacks:** `AbortController`, `setInterval`, `aria-busy`, and `prefers-reduced-motion` are universally supported. If `scrollbar-gutter: stable` or `text-wrap: pretty` is unsupported in legacy browsers, padding and `line-height: 1.6` preserve clean visual framing.

guides.title: Three-Act Value Storytelling
guides.description: Replace fragmented floating claim badges with cohesive three-act value stories moving from Act I Craft & Provenance to Act II Empirical Truth and Act III Psychological Safety.
triggers: eliminating cluttered pill clouds or floating claim chips on cards
structuring product, model, or action cards to build human trust
connecting verifiable metrics directly to safety guarantees
guides.overview: Scattering isolated claim pills across a screen—`[0% Fee]`, `[1-Tap Hold]`, `[Verified]`, `[Local]`—forces the user's working memory to assemble a fragmented puzzle across five or more visual fixations. Replace floating badge clutter with a disciplined three-act value narrative on each card: **Craft & Provenance**, **Empirical Truth**, and **Psychological Safety**.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Ban unanchored floating claim badges

Never stack three or more disconnected marketing pills on a card or hero strip without causal prose connecting them. Every quantitative or safety claim must sit inside a unified narrative flow paired with its proof anchor.

### Rule 2: Follow the three-act causal arc inside `<= 45` words

Structure every primary card narrative across three sequential beats:
- **Act I (Craft & Provenance):** Who created or verified the item and its real-world context.
- **Act II (Empirical Truth):** Transparent pricing, measured outcome, or exact operating metric with units.
- **Act III (Psychological Safety):** Clear reversibility, cancel window, or zero-penalty guarantee.

### Rule 3: Match narrative density to scan horizon

Keep Tier-1 glance chips at `<= 14` words (`<= 300ms` scan) and Tier-2 three-act card narratives at `<= 45` words (`< 3s` scan), linking deeper numerical formulas to an expandable disclosure or companion rail.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** bind Act II metrics to verifiable proofs (lot IDs, direct pricing arithmetic, measurable latency) rather than vague adjectives.
- **DO** finish every transactional card on Act III (Psychological Safety) right next to the primary CTA so risk anxiety is resolved before the click.
- **DO** keep card word budgets tight (`<= 45` words across the three acts) so the entire arc scans in one pass.
- **DON'T** render orphaned floating pill rows (`[Verified] [0% Fee] [Fast] [Safe]`) disconnected from human explanation.
- **DON'T** leak internal narrative labels like "Act I: Provenance" or "CVSM Tier 2" into customer-facing headings; use natural domain cues like `Provenance`, `Direct Value`, and `Safety Guarantee`.
- **DON'T** bury cancellation or refund safety terms inside fine-print footer links when the decision happens on the card.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
- **DOM & Playwright assertions:**
  - Count detached status badges inside `.three-act-card` and verify each card holds `<= 2` status chips while expressing all three narrative beats (`Provenance`, `Direct Value` / quantitative truth, `Safety Guarantee`).
  - Assert total narrative copy inside `.three-act-arc` stays `<= 45` words and `maxWordsPerSentence <= 18`.
  - Check responsive layout at `390px` width to ensure `.three-act-arc li` stacks into a single column with zero text clipping or horizontal overflow.
- **Browser fallbacks:** `color-mix(in srgb, ...)` can be paired with a fallback `border-top: 1px solid currentColor` or static neutral rule prior to the `color-mix` line for legacy CSS engines.

guides.title: Anchored Floating Match Windows (Choice 2B) & Hidden-Until-Found Search
guides.description: Preserve zero normal-flow displacement (DeltaB_inflow = 0px) by keeping in-flow details closed during typing and projecting live search matches and hidden="until-found" previews into CSS-anchored top-layer floating match windows.
triggers: preventing search inputs or focus suggestions from pushing page content downward
projecting live search matches next to an active search input in the top layer
making collapsed card specs and hidden content searchable without auto-opening accordions
stopping single-result grid filters from stretching cards across the entire row
guides.overview: When typing into a search box auto-expands in-flow `<details>` drawers or reveals normal-flow helper bars (`display: none -> flex`), content below shifts downward (`DeltaB_inflow > 0px`), disorienting the user right at the focal point. Under **Choice 2B**, in-flow disclosures remain closed while typing (`DeltaB_inflow = 0px`), live matches and collapsed `[hidden="until-found"]` snippets project into a **CSS-Anchored Top-Layer Floating Match Window** directly below the search input, and card grids preserve fixed column tracks.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Keep input envelopes and in-flow disclosures constant (`DeltaB_inflow = 0px`)

Maintain identical block padding on search wrappers across rest, `:focus`, and `:not(:placeholder-shown)`. Never auto-open in-flow `<details>` accordions or insert normal-flow suggestion banners during search input.

### Rule 2: Project live matches into a CSS-anchored top-layer `popover="manual"` window

Render live search results, quick-browse chips, and hidden spec previews inside `<div id="floating-match-window" popover="manual">` tethered directly below the active `<input type="search">` via `anchor-name`, `position-anchor`, `position-area: block-end span-inline-end`, and `position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, flip-inline`. Use `popover="manual"` (not `auto`) so typing never loses focus and external keyboard/outside-click handlers stay clean.

### Rule 3: Preserve grid tracks during filtering (`repeat(auto-fill)` + `align-items: start`)

Use `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, 280px), 1fr))` instead of `auto-fit` so filtering down to `1` matching card never stretches it across `100%` width, and set `align-items: start` so opening one card's `<details>` never stretches sibling cards in the same row.

### Rule 4: Support `hidden="until-found"` with `beforematch` and IME composition safety

Tag deep spec panels with `hidden="until-found"` (without `display: none`) and listen for `beforematch` so browser Find-in-Page (`Ctrl+F` / `Cmd+F`) and fragment links reveal them cleanly. Defer live match filtering during IME composition (`compositionstart` / `compositionend`), and fall back to `getBoundingClientRect()` coordinates when CSS Anchor Positioning is unavailable.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** keep padding, borders, and sibling heights invariant when a search input receives focus or input (`DeltaB_inflow = 0px`).
- **DO** apply `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, 280px), 1fr))` and `align-items: start` on filterable grids to prevent card width ballooning and sibling row stretch.
- **DO** put `hidden="until-found"` on an inner child wrapper (`.c2b-spec-body`), never directly on a padded/bordered parent or alongside `display: none`.
- **DON'T** auto-expand in-flow `<details>` accordions inside the document flow during live search keystrokes.
- **DON'T** omit the `getBoundingClientRect()` fallback for browsers without CSS Anchor Positioning (`position-area`).
guides.verificationMarkdown:
1. **Zero In-Flow Displacement (`DeltaB_inflow = 0px`):** Measure `.c2b-card-grid` `getBoundingClientRect().top` before focusing `#c2b-search-input`, after focusing, and after typing `"thermal"`. Assert `Math.abs(afterTop - beforeTop) === 0` and verify all `<details>` in `.c2b-card-grid` remain `open === false`.
2. **Track Conservation Check:** Hide all cards except 1 and verify the remaining `.c2b-card` maintains `<= 50%` container width inside a wide (`1200px`) desktop grid (`auto-fill`, not `auto-fit`).
3. **Overlay Dismissal Check:** Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or click `#c2b-close-window` and confirm `#c2b-match-window` closes cleanly (`matches(':popover-open') === false`).

Fallbacks: When `CSS.supports('position-area', 'block-end span-inline-end')` is false (Firefox / Safari), `positionFallback()` anchors the top-layer popover right below `input.getBoundingClientRect().bottom`. When `onbeforematch` is absent, unwrap `hidden="until-found"` inside the `<details>` container so content remains searchable inside native `<details>`.

guides.title: Expertise-Graduated Scaffolding & Fast-Track Overrides
guides.description: Graduate AI onboarding hints, explanation verbosity, micro-density modes, and keyboard fast-track overrides from novice guidance to compact expert views without leaking meta-rubric chrome.
triggers: adapting onboarding hints and explanation verbosity as users advance across workflow stages
letting experienced users bypass sequential tutorials via a reversible fast-track override
scaling interface density between standard guided mode and compact analytical mode
preventing internal rubric labels or evaluation jargon from leaking into hints
guides.overview: Static onboarding banners annoy experienced practitioners on day 30, while stripping all help leaves first-time visitors lost on day 1. Graduate scaffolding cleanly across expertise stages: surface full plain-English hints during initial stages, compress completed guidance into compact summaries once stage mastery (`stage >= 4`) or fast-track override activates, and strip every trace of internal rubric jargon.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Modulate density and hint verbosity by active proficiency stage

Track proficiency explicitly through discrete workflow milestones (`stage 1..5`) or an explicit practitioner mode toggle:

- **Guided Mode (`stage 1–3`):** Render `standard` comfortable padding, active prerequisite focus indicator, and complete plain-English orientation hints (`graduation-state="ACTIVE_PRIMARY"`).
- **Graduated Expert Mode (`stage >= 4` or Fast-Track Active):** Switch zone density to `compact` or `analytical` (`--density-mode: compact`), collapse Stage-1 walkthrough boxes into single-line status cues (`graduation-state="GRADUATED_COMPACT_SUMMARY"`), and expose keyboard command palettes (`Cmd+K` / `Ctrl+K` with `<= 50ms` filter response).

### Rule 2: Provide a reversible 1-tap Fast-Track Override

Never trap returning practitioners behind locked sequential steps. Offer an explicit `[Unlock All Steps]` / `[Restore Guided View]` toggle (`aria-pressed`) so advanced users can bypass tutorial gating immediately while preserving a one-click path back to guided hints.

### Rule 3: Adapt explanations to selected user role (`aria-pressed` lens)

Offer 2–3 domain-authentic role pills (e.g., `First Responder`, `Coordinator`, `Auditor`) that re-prioritize relevant sections (`PRIMARY_FOVEAL` vs `SECONDARY_STAGED`) with non-color status symbols (`● Active`, `◐ Staged`) and `forced-colors: active` borders.

### Rule 4: Enforce zero meta-rubric leakage

Scaffolding copy must explain user actions in everyday terms. Reject internal rubric phrases (`2nd-Order`, `3rd-Order`, `Horizon 1`, `Choice 1A`, `Choice 2B`, `UI-IR`, `Salsa`, `MECE`, `Gradient`) across every hint, badge, and status bar.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** keep `[Unlock All Steps]` and `[Restore Guided View]` reversible in one click (`aria-pressed`) without losing unsaved form inputs.
- **DO** include non-color glyphs (`●`, `◐`, `✓`) and explicit `@media (forced-colors: active)` rules on graduated state banners.
- **DO** verify every hint sentence uses plain human language (`<= 18` words) free of compiler/rubric labels.
- **DON'T** abruptly delete helpful summaries when a user advances; collapse them cleanly into a 1-line compact banner with an opt-back toggle.
- **DON'T** lock keyboard-only fast-track shortcuts onto modified single letters while focus is inside `<input>`, `<textarea>`, or `<select>`.
guides.verificationMarkdown:
1. **Graduation State Toggle:** Click `#btn-fast-track` in Playwright and verify `data-density-mode` switches `standard -> compact`, `.hint-expanded` becomes hidden, `.hint-compact` is visible, and clicking again restores `ACTIVE_PRIMARY`.
2. **Meta-Rubric Leakage Audit:** Run regex `/2nd-Order|3rd-Order|Horizon 1|Choice 1A|Choice 2B|UI-IR|MECE|Salsa/i` against rendered scaffolding text and assert `0` matches.
3. **Forced-Colors Parity:** Emulate `forcedColors: 'active'` and assert active pills remain distinguishable via border thickness/system keywords.

Fallbacks: Style queries (`@container style(--density-mode: compact)`) work progressively in Chromium/Safari; pairing them with zero-specificity `:where([data-density-mode="compact"])` rules ensures identical compact rendering in Firefox and older engines.

guides.title: Happy-Path Value Payoff Disclosure & Halved Density Budgets
guides.description: Co-locate concrete 6-step happy-path outcome payoffs beside interactive workflows inside halved resting density budgets (HD1-HD6), 8-role typographic hierarchy, and soft-edge previews.
triggers: reducing dense multi-step pages by 50% or more without losing functional capability
showing users the concrete end payoff alongside a multi-step calculator or planner
enforcing a strict monotonic 8-role typographic hierarchy across every section
previewing long comparison tables cleanly with soft-edge fade and expandable overflow
guides.overview: Showing raw configuration inputs without the human payoff makes multi-step tools feel tedious, while packing every instruction, comparison row, and footnote onto the screen at rest creates exhausting ink walls. Co-locate a concrete **6-Step Happy-Path Companion** ending in an explicit **Core Value Payoff** (`58% / 42%` split stage) while cutting resting page ink and word load by `>= 50%` (`HD1..HD6`) under a constant 8-role typographic scale.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Co-locate a 6-step Happy-Path Companion ending in a concrete payoff

Inside interactive workflows (calculators, planners, account onboarding), render an adjacent `<aside class="happy-path-companion-card">` (`58% / 42%` at `@container (min-width: 680px)`) with a numbered `<ol>` of 6 concise steps culminating in Step 6 (`data-happy-path-payoff="true"`, pill `Core Value Payoff`) describing the real-world human reward. Highlight completed steps via `data-*` state attributes with `0px` box-size change.

### Rule 2: Halve resting text ink density (`HD1` / `HD4`)

Fold secondary walkthrough details, overflow cards (`4..N`), and long methodology notes into native `<details>` disclosures capped at `<= 44` words per panel. For large comparison tables, show only the top 3 resting rows with a subtle bottom `mask-image` soft-edge fade and an explicit toggle (`Show all N rows`) to reveal the rest without reflowing unrelated bands.

### Rule 3: Lock the 8-Role Constant Typographic Hierarchy (`HD3`)

Enforce strictly descending sizes across every section (`h1 > h2 > subtitle > button > h3 > h4 > p >= 14.2px (line-height >= 1.48) > microtext`), include `<meta name="text-scale" content="scale">`, keep fluid `clamp()` ranges within `max <= 2.5 * min` (WCAG 1.4.4), apply `text-wrap: balance` only on unboxed headings, `text-wrap: pretty` on paragraphs, and `text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic` on microtext badges.
guides.guidelinesMarkdown:
- **DO** include `<meta name="text-scale" content="scale">` in `<head>` and avoid overriding root `html` font-size in pixels so OS text scaling works cleanly.
- **DO** keep Step 6 (`data-happy-path-payoff="true"`) phrased as a tangible human benefit ("Show up relaxed and prepared"), not an internal feature metric.
- **DO** cap resting `<details>` explanation panels at `<= 44` words each and soft-fade truncated comparison previews via `mask-image`.
- **DON'T** break monotonic typographic descent (`h2 > subtitle > button > h3 > p >= 14.2px > micro`) inside any section.
- **DON'T** animate step completion by changing borders from `1px` to `4px` or altering padding, which shifts sibling items; use `box-shadow: inset` or color updates instead (`0px` displacement).
guides.verificationMarkdown:
1. **Monotonic Font Scale Check (Playwright):** Measure `parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize)` across `.hd-h2`, `.hd-subtitle`, `.hd-btn`, `.hd-h3`, `p`, and `.hd-micro` and assert strictly non-increasing values with `p >= 14.2px`.
2. **Payoff & Zero-Shift Check:** Verify `[data-happy-path-payoff="true"]` exists inside `.happy-path-companion-card`, click `#btn-save-plan-step`, and assert step list `height` changes by `0px`.
3. **Resting Density Check:** Assert overflow table rows start hidden (`data-expanded="false"`) and visible resting word count stays compact.

Fallbacks: Browsers without `text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic` or `mask-image` ignore those properties gracefully while keeping full semantic table rows, clean padding, and clear expansion buttons intact.

guides.title: Progressive Comprehension and Instructional Design
guides.description: Structure complex interfaces around co-located 3-order educational companions, expertise-graduated scaffolding, happy-path payoff checklists, and zero-displacement Choice 2B search windows.
triggers: helping novice users understand complex AI or technical interfaces on first exposure
keeping resting pages clean while preserving deep guidance and searchability
adapting onboarding hints and verbosity as users gain expertise
preventing search inputs or filter interactions from pushing page layout downward
guides.overview:
Complex tools fail novices when they bury foundational explanations inside distant documentation tabs, and fail experts when they clutter resting screens with permanent tutorial banners. Progressive Comprehension (`D29`) solves both simultaneously by pairing spatial co-location (`58%–60%` subject beside a `40%–42%` sticky companion) with halved resting information density (`>= 50%` reduction via native `<details>`, `[popover]`, and `hidden="until-found"`), expertise-graduated scaffolding, and `0px` inflow layout displacement.

Use this discipline whenever an interface must teach unfamiliar concepts cleanly on first exposure while staying fast, searchable, and uncluttered for returning practitioners.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
Select the specialized guide that fits the comprehension challenge:

### Rule 1: First-time users cannot decode a complex subject (`split-stage-3order-companion`)

Apply when interactive calculators, configuration tools, or technical items need immediate plain-English explanation without pushing content below the fold. Render a sticky `58%–60%` subject column beside a `40%–42%` educational companion: Tier 1 layperson anatomy open by default, with Tier 2 multi-actor coordination and Tier 3 long-horizon sustainment folded inside native `<details>`.

### Rule 2: Onboarding prose slows down experienced operators (`expertise-graduated-scaffolding`)

Apply when returning users already know the workflow and want compact controls or keyboard fast-tracks. Graduate hint verbosity across expertise stages (`Onboarding -> Guided -> Graduated Compact`) with a reversible fast-track toggle while stripping all internal meta-rubric labels.

### Rule 3: Multi-step workflows obscure the end benefit (`happy-path-value-payoff-disclosure`)

Apply when users see isolated form controls or rows without understanding how the steps combine. Co-locate a 6-step concrete happy-path checklist culminating in an explicit Core Value Payoff inside halved resting density budgets (`HD1..HD6`) and a constant 8-role typographic hierarchy.

### Rule 4: Typing or filtering jumps the page layout (`anchored-floating-match-windows`)

Apply whenever a user focuses a search or prompt field or filters a card grid. Enforce Choice 2B (`DeltaB_inflow = 0px`): keep in-flow `<details>` collapsed at rest, project live matches and `hidden="until-found"` previews into a CSS-anchored top-layer floating window, and lock grid tracks with `repeat(auto-fill, ...)`.

A **Split-Stage 3-Order Companion** solves this by placing a sticky `40%–42%` educational `<aside>` directly beside a `58%–60%` interactive subject column, keeping a complete plain-English first exposure open at rest while disclosing group coordination and long-horizon sustainment inside native `<details>`.
guides.decisionRulesMarkdown:
### Rule 1: Enforce `58%–60%` Subject / `40%–42%` Sticky Companion Geometry

On desktop (`@media (min-width: 900px)` / `@container (min-width: 820px)`), render the primary interactive subject or `#1 Query Match` inside `minmax(0, 58fr)` (`58%–60%`) and the `<aside class="cc-education-companion-card">` inside `minmax(300px, 42fr)` (`40%–42%`), with `position: sticky; top: 5.25rem` and `align-self: start` on both columns. Collapse cleanly to one column below `900px`.

### Rule 2: Layer Three Epistemic Comprehension Orders (`Tier 1 -> Tier 2 -> Tier 3`)

- **Tier 1 (Default Open — Complete First Exposure):** Assume zero specialist background. Open with a plain-English hook, a core value proposition, and a 4-part `<dl>` Subject Anatomy translating technical terms into everyday analogies.
- **Tier 2 (Collapsed `<details>` — Contextual Group Coordination):** Reframe comprehension around how a venue lead, team coordinator, or coach helps untrained participants understand and act inside crowded or multi-actor settings.
- **Tier 3 (Collapsed `<details>` — Environmental & Operational Sustainment):** Reframe comprehension around how a steward preserves readiness, physical integrity, lighting visibility, and calibration over long timelines.

### Rule 3: Synchronize dynamically with `0px` focal jump (`withViewportPin`)

When users click module switcher pills (`aria-pressed`), pick a filter chip, or select a subject item, update the companion's Tier 1–3 content immediately in place. Wrap DOM updates in synchronous trigger-relative viewport pinning (`window.scrollBy(0, afterTop - beforeTop)`), so the clicked control never moves under the pointer (`DeltaY_focal = 0px`).

### Rule 4: Quarantine epistemic taxonomy labels off user-facing copy

Never print internal architecture strings (`Tier 1`, `1st-Order`, `2nd-Order`, `3rd-Order`, `CC1`) in the rendered UI. Translate each tier into its real domain role label (`First-Time Resident`, `Campus Coordinator`, `Site Steward`).
